meta.title: Fractal Studio
meta.description: Explore two-dimensional fractal maps in the browser: native C++ compute, reproducible image recipes, high-precision deep zoom and a creator marketplace.

hero.title: Explore infinite complexity on the complex plane
hero.subtitle: One drag takes you into the boundary of the Mandelbrot set. Rendering runs on a native C++ compute backend, and every image keeps a reproducible parameter recipe, so you can return to the same coordinate whenever you like.

intro.title: A reproducible fractal imaging system
intro.body1: Fractal Studio splits interactive exploration from final rendering. The browser owns the viewport, the parameters and a low-resolution preview; the real work goes to a private native C++ service. You keep instant feedback while dragging, and full precision when exporting.
intro.body2: Every exploration is stored as a canonical parameter recipe rather than an isolated picture. Re-rendering the same recipe later produces the same result, and it scales straight up to export size.

browser.note: Viewport control, parameter editing, live preview and downloads.

meta.title: Tutorial · Fractal Studio
meta.description: Learn Fractal Studio in six steps: pick a formula, explore the viewport, the Julia dual plane, iteration depth, colouring, and exporting and listing your work.

tutorial.title: One complete piece in six steps
tutorial.lede: This guide follows the order of the workbench panels. You do not have to read it end to end — open the workbench and follow along. Each step closes with the mistake people usually hit.

mode.name: Choose an image mode and a formula
mode.body1: The first panel is the image mode. A plain map renders the whole set on the parameter plane. Julia fixes a complex constant c and renders the matching dynamical plane instead. The pair and multi transitions take two-dimensional slices between formulas, and custom formula and formula sequence let you define the iteration yourself.
mode.body2: In plain map mode you can swap the formula freely — {variants} are built in, from the classic Mandelbrot to Tricorn, Burning Ship, Celtic, and the transcendental sin, cos and exp family. Each one carries a line describing its geometry.
mode.tip: Frame the view with Mandelbrot first, then switch formulas: the coordinate and zoom carry over, and the same location often looks nothing alike under a different formula.

navigate.name: Pan and zoom to explore
navigate.body1: The canvas is directly manipulable. Drag to pan; use the wheel or a two-finger pinch to zoom. Zoom is anchored on the pointer or on the midpoint between your fingers, so the structure you are watching stays put.
navigate.body2: The crosshair marks the current viewport centre, and the badge in the corner shows the export frame size. Zooming applies a CSS transform for instant feedback while the real recomputation follows, so dragging never stalls.
navigate.tip: If the image turns mushy or blocky once you are deep, that is usually not a zoom limit — it means iterations are too low or the scalar precision needs raising. See step 04.

julia.name: The Julia dual plane and picking c
julia.body1: Julia mode splits the canvas in two: the parameter plane on the left, the matching dynamical plane on the right. Click anywhere on the parameter plane to set the complex constant c, and the right pane recomputes at once.
julia.body2: The chosen c stays marked with a ring on the parameter plane. The two panes pan and zoom independently, so you can nudge c along the boundary on one side while magnifying the detail on the other.
julia.tip: Values of c near the boundary of the set are usually the interesting ones: c inside gives solid regions, and c too far outside shatters the Julia set into dust.

depth.name: Iteration depth and orbit metrics
depth.body1: Maximum iterations decides how many steps run before a point is declared escaped. The deeper you zoom, the finer the boundary and the more iterations it needs; too few shows up as detail flattening into blocks of solid colour.
depth.body2: The orbit metric decides which property of the orbit drives the colour: escape time is the standard, minimum and maximum magnitude reveal filaments inside the set, and the orbit envelope gives broader texture. The scalar type can be fp32, fp64 or fx64 — more precision holds detail together under deep zoom.
depth.tip: Iterations and render time scale together. Find the location at a low iteration count, then raise it once the composition is settled and submit the real render.

coloring.name: Palettes and gradients
coloring.body1: There are {colorMaps} built-in palettes, from grayscale to Viridis, Inferno and Spectral. On top of that sits the colouring mode: direct stays faithful to the raw metric, full histogram equalization reveals global structure, and centre-weighted equalization suits exploring around a subject.
coloring.body2: For full control, switch to a custom gradient: place your own stops and tune cycles, phase and wrap. Note that a built-in palette and a custom gradient are mutually exclusive — once the gradient is on it takes over, and it requires the direct colouring mode.
coloring.tip: The preview in the workbench can look brighter than the exported master, because the two use different sampling sizes. Tune the gradient against an export, not against the preview alone.

publish.name: Export a PNG and list it
publish.body1: In the export panel, pick a preset frame or type a custom size — up to {maxEdge} px per edge — then submit the render. Rendering is asynchronous with live progress; when it finishes the piece lands in your library and the PNG master is downloadable.
publish.body2: To sell, first request a creator profile on the payouts page with a handle and a display name. Then create a listing draft for the piece from your library, set a price and publish it to the marketplace. Buyer payments are confirmed by an Alipay callback, after which they can download the master and you keep a revenue share.
publish.tip: Free accounts have a limited number of exports; membership removes the cap. Publishing also waits on a watermarked public preview being generated, so a fresh draft may not be publishable for a moment.

meta.title: Help and FAQ · Fractal Studio
meta.description: Fractal Studio FAQ: accounts and sign-in, membership and payment, rendering and export, marketplace and payouts, mobile use and troubleshooting.

help.title: Frequently asked questions
help.lede: Grouped by topic. If you are after the steps rather than a fix, the tutorial is the better place to start.

password.a: At least 12 characters. There is no forced mix of character classes beyond that, though a longer password is obviously stronger.

session.q: Why did another tab say my sign-in changed?
session.a: The session is shared across one browser window. If you sign in as a different account or sign out in another tab, the others notice and tell you, so you do not keep working under the wrong account.

reset.a: There is no self-service password reset yet. If you cannot sign in, contact the site administrator.

what.a: Classic map rendering, Julia exploration, every transition mode, and unlimited PNG export. It is a one-time ¥29, not a subscription.

pay.a: Alipay for now. Once payment completes, an Alipay callback confirms it and the entitlement takes effect immediately.

pending.a: The callback can lag briefly. Wait a moment and refresh, or check the order status under Purchases. If the order still says awaiting payment you can retry; if it says a payment is already pending, do not order again.

quota.q: How many exports does a free account get?
quota.a: Free accounts have an export cap, and exporting past it reports the quota as exhausted. Membership has no cap.

slow.q: How long does a render take?
slow.a: Mostly a function of iteration count and output size, both of which scale roughly linearly with time. Find the composition at a low iteration count, then raise it for the real render.

size.a: Up to {maxEdge} px per edge. Use a preset frame or enter your own width and height.

brightness.q: Why is my export darker than the preview?
brightness.a: Preview and export sample at different sizes, so the same gradient reads differently in each. Judge colour from an export; tuning against the preview alone tends to come out dark.

deep.q: Is there a zoom depth limit?
deep.a: The limit comes from numeric precision, not from a fixed zoom level. When you go deep, raise the iteration count and switch the scalar type to fp64 or fx64 — running out of precision shows up as blocky patches and flattened detail.

become.q: How do I become a creator?
become.a: Fill in a handle and display name on the payouts page. There is no review step. Once the creator role is granted, the listing action appears in your library.

handle.q: What are the rules for a creator handle?
handle.a: 3 to 32 characters, lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, and unique across the site. It appears in your public profile URL, so it is worth settling on one.

publish.q: Why can't I publish a fresh listing draft?
publish.a: Publishing waits on a watermarked public preview being generated for the piece. The publish action stays disabled until it is ready — wait a moment and refresh.

payout.a: Once a buyer's payment is confirmed, your share accumulates in the available balance. Submit a payout request with your receiving code on the payouts page. Only one request can be pending at a time.

zoom.q: How do I zoom the map on a phone?
zoom.a: Pinch with two fingers, anchored on the midpoint between them. One finger drags to pan, and moving two fingers together pans while zooming. A double tap also zooms in one step.

nav.a: On narrow screens it collapses into a drawer. Tap the panel icon in the top left to open it; it closes itself once you pick a page.

canvas.q: Why is the canvas small on my phone?
canvas.a: The canvas fits the screen width at the export frame's aspect ratio, so the page never scrolls sideways. Zoom in to inspect detail rather than scrolling horizontally.

noPreview.a: The first preview takes a moment to generate. If it stays in the computing state, check your connection and reload. More complex parameters and higher iteration counts both make previews slower.

noPayment.a: Order status is driven by the Alipay callback, which can lag. Check Purchases for the latest state rather than paying again; if it stays in an exception state, contact an administrator to reconcile it.

tabs.q: Actions fail even though I appear signed in.
tabs.a: After switching accounts across tabs, an older tab may be holding a session that no longer applies. Reload that tab to resynchronise.

more.body: Not covered here? The tutorial walks the whole flow, and once you sign up you can try it directly in the workbench.

studio.title: Fractal Studio
studio.subtitle: Explore mathematical maps, Julia sets, axis transitions and safe custom orbit programs; export the current composition as a reproducible PNG.
studio.memberLocked: Member exclusive — upgrade in Membership page

modeNotes.map: Explore any built-in two-dimensional map in the parameter plane.
modeNotes.julia: Render the dynamical plane for a fixed complex constant c.
modeNotes.transitionPair: Take a two-dimensional slice between two axis-lifted formulas.
modeNotes.transitionMulti: Blend a weighted schedule of up to four axis-lifted formulas into one image.
modeNotes.formula: Use the bounded Orbit Program DSL; no native code is compiled in the browser or service.
modeNotes.sequence: Repeat several safe formulas for specified iteration spans. This changes the orbit itself, not only the output color.

studio.juliaSelectInstruction: Use the left parameter plane to choose c. Both views pan and zoom independently; only the right Julia plane is exported.
studio.juliaPickerHint: Click a point to choose c; drag or zoom to inspect the parameter plane.
studio.juliaOutputHint: The Julia set for the selected c. This viewport is the exported image.
studio.formulaExamplesHint: Click to load an expression. An unchanged example uses its equivalent optimized built-in implementation; editing it turns it into a custom DSL formula.
studio.formulaHint: z and c are complex, i is the imaginary unit, and n is the current iteration. Functions include sin, cos, tan, exp, log, sqrt, abs, conj, sinh, cosh, tanh, real and imag. Unverified formulas are colored by the iteration where arithmetic overflows; finite pixels run to the iteration limit.
studio.sequenceHint: Steps repeat in order. A span of 3 applies that formula for three iterations before advancing.
studio.transitionHint: Only formulas with a defined axis lift are offered. This is a two-dimensional result and exports exactly like the ordinary map.
studio.centerAlwaysVisible: center is retained in every recipe

canvas.hintTouch: one-finger drag: pan · two fingers: zoom
canvas.selectHint: click: choose c · drag: pan · wheel: zoom
canvas.selectHintTouch: tap: choose c · one-finger drag: pan · two fingers: zoom

studio.compositionHint: The preview uses the same aspect ratio as the export frame. Output dimensions are bounded to 64–4096 px per side.
studio.upgradeForUnlimited: Upgrade to membership for unlimited exports
studio.customGradientHint: Custom gradients use direct coloring. Stop positions, repeat behavior, interior and invalid colors are saved in the recipe.

direct.name: Direct
direct.description: Map the raw metric directly to color. Fast and faithful, but dense regions can bunch into a narrow color range.

eq_full.name: Full histogram equalization
eq_full.description: Redistribute values using the whole image histogram. Reveals global structure but the palette can shift when the viewport changes.

eq_center.name: Center-weighted equalization
eq_center.description: Equalize with more influence from the central region. Useful while navigating a focal structure and less dominated by outer pixels.

escape.name: Escape time
escape.description: Color by how quickly the orbit leaves the bailout radius; the standard set boundary view.

min_abs.name: Minimum magnitude
min_abs.description: Record the closest approach to the origin across the orbit, exposing internal filaments.

max_abs.name: Maximum magnitude
max_abs.description: Record the greatest orbit magnitude, emphasizing growth and outer-field structure.

envelope.name: Orbit envelope
envelope.description: Summarize the orbit's radial envelope to reveal broader dynamical texture.

min_pairwise_dist.name: Minimum pairwise distance
min_pairwise_dist.description: Measure near-recurrence between sampled orbit points. More expensive and controlled by the pairwise cap.

mandel_ship_agree.name: Mandelbrot / Ship agreement
mandel_ship_agree.description: Compare two built-in orbit classifications to visualize where their behavior agrees.

mandelbrot.name: Mandelbrot
mandelbrot.description: The canonical quadratic map z² + c and the reference point for the family.

tricorn.name: Tricorn
tricorn.description: A conjugated quadratic map with threefold, reflection-rich geometry.

burning_ship.name: Burning Ship
burning_ship.description: Folds both complex components before iteration, producing sharp hulls and flame-like detail.

celtic.name: Celtic
celtic.description: A folded quadratic variant with interlocking bands and knot-like boundaries.

heart.name: Heart
heart.description: A directional fold that produces rounded lobes and asymmetric heart-like regions.

buffalo.name: Buffalo
buffalo.description: A two-axis folded family with branching silhouettes and dense boundary texture.

perp_buffalo.name: Perpendicular Buffalo
perp_buffalo.description: A perpendicular fold of the Buffalo family with altered reflection symmetry.

celtic_ship.name: Celtic Ship
celtic_ship.description: Combines Celtic and Burning Ship folds into layered, angular coastlines.

mandelceltic.name: Mandelceltic
mandelceltic.description: A Mandelbrot–Celtic hybrid that keeps the main cardioid context while folding local detail.

perp_ship.name: Perpendicular Ship
perp_ship.description: A perpendicular Burning Ship fold with distinct directional ridges.

sin_z.name: Sine map
sin_z.description: Uses the complex sine function in the orbit, creating periodic lobes across the plane.

cos_z.name: Cosine map
cos_z.description: Uses complex cosine dynamics, with repeating bands and strong imaginary-axis growth.

exp_z.name: Exponential map
exp_z.description: Complex exponential dynamics produce rapidly growing, repeating structures.

sinh_z.name: Hyperbolic sine
sinh_z.description: Hyperbolic sine dynamics combine exponential growth with odd symmetry.

cosh_z.name: Hyperbolic cosine
cosh_z.description: Hyperbolic cosine dynamics combine exponential growth with even symmetry.

tan_z.name: Tangent map
tan_z.description: Complex tangent introduces poles and repeating domains with abrupt boundaries.

classic_cos.name: Classic cosine
classic_cos.description: Continuous cosine channels cycle through deep blue, amber and pale highlights.
classic_cos.cost: low cost; periodic colors can hide absolute iteration differences.

mod17.name: Modulo 17
mod17.description: A deliberately discrete 17-step palette that exposes iteration bands.
mod17.bestFor: teaching escape counts and spotting band boundaries.
mod17.cost: very clear bands, but little smooth tonal depth.

hsv_wheel.name: HSV wheel
hsv_wheel.description: Cycles through the full hue wheel at near-constant saturation.
hsv_wheel.bestFor: periodic metrics and visually separating adjacent bands.
hsv_wheel.cost: hue changes are not perceptually uniform in brightness.

tri765.name: Triangular 765
tri765.description: A long triangular RGB cycle with crisp rises and falls in each channel.
tri765.bestFor: high-frequency iteration structure and retro scientific plots.
tri765.cost: strong contrast may dominate subtle geometry.

grayscale.name: Grayscale
grayscale.description: A neutral black-to-white ramp with no hue encoding.
grayscale.bestFor: shape study, print, masks and later compositing.
grayscale.cost: lowest visual ambiguity, but cannot separate multiple value classes by hue.

hs_rainbow.name: Hidden-structure rainbow
hs_rainbow.description: A broad scientific rainbow tuned for non-escape orbit fields.
hs_rainbow.bestFor: minimum magnitude, envelope and hidden-structure metrics.
hs_rainbow.cost: colorful and legible, though not luminance-uniform.

inferno.name: Inferno
inferno.description: A dark perceptual ramp through violet, red, orange and pale yellow.
inferno.bestFor: fine structure on dark backgrounds and monotonic magnitude reading.
inferno.cost: high values receive strong visual emphasis.

viridis.name: Viridis
viridis.description: A perceptual violet-blue-green-yellow ramp with steadily increasing lightness.
viridis.bestFor: measurement-oriented images and broad value ranges.
viridis.cost: restrained mood; cyclic boundaries are less obvious.

twilight.name: Twilight
twilight.description: A cyclic light–violet–navy–magenta palette whose ends meet smoothly.
twilight.bestFor: phase-like or repeating values without a visible seam.
twilight.cost: lightness reverses, so it is not ideal for strictly ordered magnitude.

ember_blue.name: Ember blue
ember_blue.description: A project palette moving from midnight blue through cyan to amber-white.
ember_blue.bestFor: cold-to-hot contrast and finished artwork with a restrained identity.
ember_blue.cost: artistic contrast is stronger than neutral measurement.

spectral1530.name: Spectral 1530
spectral1530.description: A long multi-hue spectral cycle designed to keep many adjacent bands distinct.
spectral1530.bestFor: deep iteration ranges and dense band comparison.
spectral1530.cost: many hues can make global ordering harder to read.
